title: Listening, Clarifying & Confirming
summary: Practice active listening, asking useful clarification questions, and confirming important information before acting.
objectives: Explain why listening is an active workplace skill.
Use clarification questions when instructions or expectations are unclear.
Confirm critical information without pretending to understand.

vocab.def: Giving focused attention to a message and working to understand its meaning before responding.
Additional information that makes an instruction, expectation, or message easier to understand.
Checking that important information or expectations have been understood correctly.
Restating information in your own words to check understanding.

sections.heading: Listening is more than staying quiet
sections.body: Active listening means paying attention to the speaker, identifying the important information, noticing uncertainty, and avoiding assumptions about what was meant.

sections.heading: Good questions reduce confusion
sections.body: When information is unclear, specific questions are usually more useful than saying only that you do not understand. Ask about the exact part that needs clarification.

sections.heading: Confirm important details
sections.body: Repeating or paraphrasing a critical instruction can prevent mistakes. Confirmation is especially useful when details affect safety, deadlines, quality, customers, or other people.

sections.heading: Do not pretend to understand
sections.body: Pretending to understand can turn a small communication gap into a larger operational problem. Asking for clarification is often a sign of responsibility.

practice.prompt: A supervisor gives you several instructions quickly and you are unsure which task is the priority. What should you do?
practice.answer: Ask which task should be completed first and confirm the priority before proceeding.

practice.prompt: You think you understand a safety-related instruction but one detail is uncertain. What is the best response?
practice.answer: Clarify the uncertain detail and confirm the instruction before acting.

quiz.question: Which response best demonstrates active listening?
options: Restating the important instruction and asking about anything unclear
Waiting quietly until the speaker stops and then guessing
Agreeing immediately even when the message is confusing
Changing the subject when too many details are provided
quiz.answer: Restating the important instruction and asking about anything unclear

lab.objective: Practice listening to workplace instructions, identifying missing information, asking clarification questions, and confirming next steps.

reflectionPrompt: Why can asking a clarification question demonstrate professionalism rather than weakness?
